title: The self that is never born and never dies

verses.tr: Contacts with the senses, O son of Kunti, bring heat and cold, pleasure and pain. They come and go; they are impermanent. Endure them, O Bharata.
verses.angle: Kunteya: a son of Kunti gets a command
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna that the soul never dies. Now he turns to the body's daily experience and tells him what to do with it.

body.text: Contacts with the senses, O son of Kunti, bring heat and cold, pleasure and pain. They come and go; they are impermanent. Endure them, O Bharata. Krishna calls him Kunteya, son of Kunti, and tells him to endure. What he must endure is the heat and cold, the pleasure and pain, that come from the senses. He adds that these experiences are impermanent, coming and going, so the wise should bear them without distress.

verses.sa: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ । समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
verses.tr: The wise person who is not shaken by these, and remains equal in pain and pleasure, becomes fit for freedom.
verses.angle: Dhiram: the steadfast person who stays even through pleasure and pain
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The previous verse said to endure heat and cold. But how? Listen to how Krishna names the person who can do it.

body.text: The wise person who is not shaken by these, and remains equal in pain and pleasure, becomes fit for freedom. Listen to the word dhiram, steadfast. It names the person who stays even through pleasure and pain, and that steadiness is what makes him fit for freedom. Krishna now asks you to look at the boundary between what is real and what is not.

verses.sa: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः । उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
verses.tr: The unreal has no being; the real has no nonbeing. Seers have understood the boundary of both.
verses.angle: Nasato and nabhavo define the real and the unreal
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now draws a hard line between what is real and what is not. Listen for the two sides of existence.

body.text: The unreal has no being; the real has no nonbeing. Seers have understood the boundary of both. Listen to the exact boundary between the unreal and the real. Nasato, what is unreal, has no permanent being, and nabhavo, the nonbeing of the real, never exists. Krishna then tells him to know the imperishable reality that pervades this whole world.

verses.sa: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् । विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित् कर्तुमर्हति ॥
verses.tr: Know that to be imperishable by which this entire world is pervaded. No one can destroy this imperishable reality.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is answering Arjuna's fear of killing. He asks him to focus on the one truth that can never be destroyed.

body.text: Know that to be imperishable by which this entire world is pervaded. No one can destroy this imperishable reality. The word is avinashi, imperishable. It is the reality that pervades the entire world, and no one has the power to destroy it. Krishna now tells Arjuna that these bodies are temporary, but the being inside them cannot be harmed.

verses.sa: अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः । अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत ॥
verses.tr: These bodies are said to be finite, but the embodied being is eternal, indestructible, and immeasurable. Therefore, fight, Arjuna.
verses.angle: Bodies end, the embodied being does not
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the imperishable soul. Now he turns back to the body and tells Arjuna what to do with it.

body.text: These bodies are said to be finite, but the embodied being is eternal, indestructible, and immeasurable. Therefore, fight, Arjuna. The verse sets up a direct pairing: the bodies are finite, but the embodied being is eternal, indestructible, and immeasurable. The command to fight follows directly from this truth. Krishna now asks Arjuna to stop thinking of the soul as either the killer or the killed.

verses.sa: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् । उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥
verses.tr: Whoever thinks this imperishable being is the killer, and whoever thinks it is killed, both do not understand. It neither kills nor is killed.
verses.angle: The self is neither killer nor killed
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna sharpens his point by rejecting both pictures of death and murder. Listen to how he frames the error.

body.text: Whoever thinks this imperishable being is the killer, and whoever thinks it is killed, both do not understand. It neither kills nor is killed. Notice how Krishna turns both statements into the same mistake. Whether you see the self as the killer or as the killed, both views miss the mark, because the self does neither. He then states the truth directly, that this being is unborn and never dies.

verses.sa: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः । अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणोन हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥
verses.tr: It is never born and never dies. It did not come into being, and it will not cease. Unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient, it is not destroyed when the body is destroyed.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: How do you end what has no beginning? Krishna answers with a list of what the self is not. Listen for the first word.

body.text: It is never born and never dies. It did not come into being, and it will not cease. Unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient, it is not destroyed when the body is destroyed. The first word Krishna speaks is ajah, unborn. The self did not come into being, and it will not cease to be again. It is beyond the cycle of birth and death. If the self is unborn, Krishna then asks what happens when the body is destroyed.

verses.sa: वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम् । कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥
verses.tr: One who knows the imperishable, eternal, unborn, and unchanging cannot think of killing or causing death.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts from anatomy to vision, asking how anyone with true sight could even think of killing.

body.text: One who knows the imperishable, eternal, unborn, and unchanging cannot think of killing or causing death. Krishna asks katham, how. If you truly see the self inside as unborn and imperishable, the very idea of killing collapses, because you cannot destroy what was never born. Krishna then gives the image of changing clothes to show what the body really is.

verses.sa: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहायनवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि । तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही ॥
verses.tr: As a person discards worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the embodied being discards worn-out bodies and enters new ones.
verses.angle: Dehi: the embodied one leaves the body
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna tells Arjuna to look past the death of the body. Listen to one word that makes the body sound like an everyday object.

body.text: As a person discards worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the embodied being discards worn-out bodies and enters new ones. Listen to one word, dehi, the embodied one. The body is not the self; it is merely a worn-out thing the embodied one leaves behind, just as a person leaves behind old clothes. Krishna now turns to what weapons and fire cannot touch, the self that never dies.

verses.sa: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः । न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥
verses.tr: Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it.
verses.angle: Nainam: the self beyond physical force
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna answers Arjuna's fear of killing by explaining what the soul is not. Listen for the four forces he names.

body.text: Weapons cannot cut it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it. Krishna names the self by saying what it is not. He does not say the soul is safe from weapons, he says weapons cannot cut it. Krishna now tells Arjuna what this self actually is, beyond all physical limits.

verses.sa: अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च । नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥
verses.tr: This embodied self cannot be cut, burned, wetted, or dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, unmoving, fixed, and timeless.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues by listing exactly what physical force cannot do to the true self. Listen for the word that describes the limits of water.

body.text: This embodied self cannot be cut, burned, wetted, or dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, unmoving, fixed, and timeless. Krishna uses the word ashosyah, undryable, to show that the inner being cannot be dried by any force. It is eternal, all-pervading, unmoving, and fixed, standing beyond the reach of any physical element. The next verse says this self is unseen and beyond thought, so Arjuna should stop grieving.

verses.tr: It is unseen, beyond thought, and said to be unchanged. Therefore, knowing it this way, you should not grieve.
verses.angle: Ayam, this: the self is unseen, unthinkable, unchanged
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks why Arjuna is grieving over bodies when the truth of the self is beyond sight and thought. Listen for three qualities of the inner reality.

body.text: It is unseen, beyond thought, and said to be unchanged. Therefore, knowing it this way, you should not grieve. Listen to the word ayam, this. It appears three times, pointing to the self, and each time it tells us the self is unseen, unthinkable, and unchanged, so grieving over it is useless. Krishna now asks what would happen if Arjuna still thought the self was born and died.

verses.sa: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् । तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
verses.tr: O mighty-armed one, even if you think this embodied being is always born and always dies, you still should not grieve like this.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna offers Arjuna a second reason to stop grieving. Listen for how Krishna meets him where he is.

body.text: O mighty-armed one, even if you think this embodied being is always born and always dies, you still should not grieve like this. Krishna does not force his own view on Arjuna. He begins with 'even then', showing he is willing to argue from Arjuna's own assumptions. Krishna now points out that death is certain for the born, and birth for the dead.

verses.sa: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च । तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥
verses.tr: For what is born, death is certain; for what dies, birth is certain. What cannot be avoided should not be grieved over.
verses.angle: Dhruvam: the certainty of birth and death
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna reminds Arjuna that the cycle of the body is fixed and asks him to stop grieving over it.

body.text: For what is born, death is certain; for what dies, birth is certain. What cannot be avoided should not be grieved over. The word dhruvam, meaning certain, is used twice here. It marks two truths that never break: the born must die, and the dead must be born again. Krishna now points out that the self is unmanifest before birth and after death.
